item.title: Naoshi Fujikura of Universal Music Japan on Japan’s Unique Superfan Culture & Global Ambitions: Billboard Global Power Players Interview
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard", your go-to podcast for the latest music industry insights. I'm your host, [Name]. Today, we're shining the spotlight on Japan's thriving music scene.
[Music transitions to a softer background tune]
Host: Universal Music Japan's president and CEO, Naoshi Fujikura, has been named to Billboard's Global Power Players list for the seventh time. In an exclusive interview with Billboard Japan, Fujikura talked about Japan's unique "superfan" culture, also known as "oshikatsu". But first, let's take a look at some impressive chart-topping numbers. In 2025, Mrs. GREEN APPLE took the top spot on both the Hot 100 and the Artist 100 Billboard Japan annual charts, and an impressive 13th place in IFPI's Global Artist Chart.
[Short music clip from Mrs. GREEN APPLE]
Host: Fujikura praised Mrs. GREEN APPLE's efforts to connect with fans across generations, saying it's amazing to see them rank alongside global artists like Taylor Swift and Lady Gaga. Japan's music market, the world's second-largest, is driving growth, with an 8.9% increase in 2025, outpacing the global market's 6.4% growth.
Host: So, what's behind this success? According to Fujikura, it's the recovery of the physical media market in Japan, combined with the rising number of people paying for streaming worldwide. But what sets Japan apart is its "oshikatsu" culture. Fujikura explains that Japanese fans are more focused on supporting their favorite artists' growth, rather than just consuming their music.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: Fujikura highlights the differences between Japanese "oshikatsu" and overseas superfans, saying that Japanese fans are more invested in their artists' success, working together to boost them into the spotlight. This culture of patronage has a long history in Japan, dating back to the worlds of kabuki and sumo.
[Music transitions to a gentle outro]
Host: That's all for today's episode of "Trending on Billboard". Thanks for tuning in. Join us next time for more insights into the music industry. [Outro music plays]
